newsitem.title: USA: U.S., India panel seeks stronger economic ties.
newsitem.headline: U.S., India panel seeks stronger economic ties.

text.p: A joint U.S.-Indian economic panel on Tuesday agreed to work to strengthen ties between the two trading partners by increasing cooperation as India continues to reform its economy.

In a joint statement issued after a meeting of the Indo-U.S. Economic/Commercial Subcommission, the two sides said the meeting provided an opportunity for comprehensive discussions on the new Indian government's economic reform program.

The Indian delegation said the government was committed to encourage large inflows of foreign investment, continuing the process of fiscal consolidation and tax reforms, as well as reforms in the financial sector.

"The Indian delegation emphasized the special importance of infrastructure and outlined policies of the government to attract private sector investment into key infrastructure sectors," the statement said.

The statement also noted that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the Securities and Exchange Board of India had held productive talks on cooperation in regulatory and enforcement matters.
"The discussions are ongoing, and the two authorities are optimistic that a memo of understanding will be signed in India in 1997," the statement said.

In a briefing for reporters after the talks, Indian Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia, who was a member of the Indian delegation, said there was discussion on how to promote investment in infrastructure.

"In order to bring the private sector into infrastructure successfully, you need the evolution of a sophisticated regulatory framework with clear transparent policies which private investors can be comfortable with," Singh said, adding "the U.S. has a lot of experience in the regulatory field,"
A great deal, he said, can be done with a simple exchange of information.
The U.S. delegation was headed by Undersecretary of State Joan Spero.
